_note: Metrics for exp-012 (issue #27 / issue #46 S1 / ADR 0024). Numbers below are transcribed as-is from runs/exp-012/{router/20260823_003810/metrics.json, eval/router_guided/eval_metrics.json, eval/unguided_rescored/eval_metrics.json, eval/oracle_guided_rescored/eval_metrics.json, compare_unguided_vs_router_guided/compare_metrics.json, compare_oracle_guided_vs_router_guided/compare_metrics.json}. No number here is derived or invented beyond simple arithmetic explicitly labelled as such. composite_score is recorded throughout but is NOT headlined (issue #40 caveat, same as exp-010/exp-011). No keep/drop recommendation is made from any of this (ADR 0028 item 2, issue #46 section 4.2) -- that is Jahid + supervisor's call.

router.chance_baseline_note: 3 classes (hop 2/3/4), 200 rows each -- uninformed guessing would score ~0.333 overall. Measured 0.3833 is only ~0.05 above that.
router.unparsed_caveat: ADR 0024 item 1a: an unparsed response is scored AS IF it predicted default_hop (2), counted in the accuracies, not dropped. Of hop=2's 175 correct rows, 123 are unparsed-defaulted (i.e. the model's response carried no readable hop count and was scored correct only because default_hop happens to equal the gold class); only 52 of the 175 came from a parsed response, out of 77 hop=2 rows the model actually answered (52/77 = 0.675 among parsed hop=2 responses -- simple arithmetic on the two counts above, not a separately computed metric). hop=3/hop=4's near-floor accuracy (0.175/0.100) is consistent with default_hop=2 giving them no free credit.

unguided_rescored.source: exp-004 unguided, predictions unchanged (runs/exp-004/20260821_222907/results.json), generated at commit 6fc4bba1b9df023625eb76a9d1d0ce6a53005858, re-scored here at this run's commit

oracle_guided_rescored.source: exp-004 oracle_guided, predictions unchanged (runs/exp-004/20260821_224805/results.json), generated at commit 6fc4bba1b9df023625eb76a9d1d0ce6a53005858, re-scored here at this run's commit

ged_fallback_bound_caveat: docs/METRICS.md: the node_cap substituted bound is NOT tight -- measured at up to +0.0588 above the optimizer's own value on the star shape at the cap boundary (ADR 0026's table). Since ged is lower-is-better, a fallback item is penalised, so unguided_rescored's single node_cap row carries a small systematic upward (worse) bias on its ged_macro relative to router_guided/oracle_guided_rescored, which have none. At 1/600 the effect on the macro average is negligible.

compare_unguided_vs_router_guided.headline: every one of the 7 bootstrap metrics and 3 McNemar metrics is non-significant

compare_oracle_guided_vs_router_guided.headline: hop_count_exact_match and ged are significant, favouring oracle; step_f1, ordered_step_accuracy, sari and chain_validity are all non-significant

composite_score.not_headlined_reason: issue #40 reference_validity defect + this pair's CI barely excludes zero at the lower bound ([+0.0001, +0.2103]), a concrete instance of the bimodal/asymmetric composite shape issue #40 documents

significance_protocol: ADR 0009 (paired bootstrap 95% CI + exact McNemar = headline) amended by ADR 0017/issue #30 (paired t-test, additive, not restated here -- see runs/exp-012/compare_*/compare_metrics.json t_test blocks for the full battery); ADR 0011 (min_items_for_significance_claim=30; both comparisons at n=600 are not underpowered on any row).
observation_not_a_recommendation: Hop guidance from a PERFECT oracle (oracle_guided vs router_guided) moves only hop_count_exact_match and ged significantly; step_f1/ordered_step_accuracy/sari/chain_validity are flat. An imperfect, prompted router (unguided vs router_guided, router overall accuracy 0.3833 vs ~0.333 chance) moves NOTHING significantly, including hop_count_exact_match itself. No keep/drop conclusion is drawn here (ADR 0028 item 2, issue #46 section 4.2 -- Jahid + supervisor's call).
